question.text: What is the lock-in period for the minimum promoter contribution in a public issue where the majority of issue proceeds are NOT earmarked for capital expenditure?

answer.text: 6 months from the date of allotment
3 years from the date of allotment
18 months from the date of allotment
12 months from the date of allotment

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the source, the minimum promoter contribution (20% of post-issue capital) is locked in for 18 months from allotment. The lock-in extends to 3 years where the majority of issue proceeds are earmarked for capital expenditure. Excess promoter holding beyond the minimum is locked in for 6 months, extending to 1 year in capex-majority issues. The Trap: The 3-year lock-in applies only where the majority of proceeds go to capex; defaulting to 3 years without checking that condition is wrong. The 6-month figure relates to excess holding, not the minimum contribution. Note: Page 82 supports the 18-month minimum lock-in and the 3-year capex extension; page 83 supports the 6-month and 1-year lock-ins for excess holdings.
